_rationale: Cash branch in growth loop must take precedence over allocation lookup. With stockAllocation=0.6 misconfigured, a naive `balances[id] *= sa*sf + (1-sa)*bf` would compute 1.34× growth → $134k pre-spending → $114k after $20k spending. The correct bypass: cash grows by (1 + cashYieldRate) = 1.04 → $104k pre-spending. cashInterest ($4k) is reinvested into the cash balance (accrue-in-account) and taxed as ordinary income, but it is NOT separately counted as spendable cash — so the full $20k spending is withdrawn from the grown $104k balance. End-of-year cash = $104k − $20k = $84k. (Counting the interest in both the balance and availableCash was the cash-double-count bug that produced $88k and masked $4k/yr of the draw.) Probability = 0%: drawing $20k/yr (20% of principal) against a 4% yield, the $100k depletes in the final year — year 5 (age 65) grows to $13,872 and falls $6,128 short of the $20k need. This depletion is the economically honest result; the prior 100% relied on the double-count.

pathValues.note: Year 1 start = year 0 end = (100k × 1.04 yield) - 20k full spending withdrawal = $84k. If bypass missing, would be ~$114k; if interest were double-counted, would be $88k.

breakdownChecks._note: Full $20k spending need pulled from cash; reinvested interest is not separate spendable income
